Approach / One direct working relationship

Work directly with
your developer.

LEVNAT is my independent development and systems-engineering practice. I work from Toronto and remotely, with scope, priorities and next steps agreed directly with you.

How an engagement works

Clear steps. Agreed scope.

  1. Describe the starting point

    Tell me what exists, who it serves and what you want to build or improve. An inquiry does not confirm an engagement.

  2. Clarify the next task

    Review requirements, access and constraints. If deeper planning is needed, agree on a paid working session before proceeding.

  3. Agree on scope and estimate

    Define deliverables, priorities, assumptions and a schedule before development or debugging starts.

  4. Build or investigate

    Implement and test the agreed work, or investigate the fault. Review findings and agree on changes to the scope rather than silently expanding it.

  5. Hand over and plan support

    Document the work and next steps. Maintenance, monitoring and support are optional, separately agreed services.

When the project needs more definition

A focused planning session.

For an idea, inherited system or technical issue that needs a closer review before implementation can be scoped.

CAD $500

A 90-minute working session, including preparation and follow-up notes. Implementation and extended investigation are not included.

Ask about a planning session

  • Project overview & constraints

    Review the goals, existing work, access needs and key technical risks.

  • A first task to scope

    Identify the next build, integration, debugging or maintenance task.

  • Written next steps

    Record priorities and open questions needed for an implementation estimate. Not a complete technical audit.

Before work starts

Practical expectations.

Timing follows the scope

There is no universal launch date. Dependencies, access, content and review time are considered in the agreed schedule.

Testing has a defined target

Browsers, devices, workflows and release requirements are agreed for the project. Test coverage and known limitations are documented at handover.

Support is explicit

Availability, included tasks and response expectations are agreed separately. Ongoing support is not implied by a one-off build.

Your next step

Start with what you know.

You do not need a finished specification to make an inquiry. Explain the goal, the existing system and what needs to happen next.
